sources.cite: AWS Lambda Developer Guide, Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: an alias points to published versions, and a weighted alias 'cannot point to $LATEST'; aws lambda update-alias --function-version N repoints an alias (and resets routing); the START log line and the ExecutedVersion dimension show which version ran; AWS SAM's AutoPublishAlias publishes a version on each change and moves the alias, with CodeDeploy DeploymentPreference shifting traffic gradually. That a plain (unweighted) alias may point to $LATEST is from memory of the aliases page (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the developer on call at Brisk Pay. The quotes API's prod stage in API Gateway invokes the Lambda function quote-engine through its alias prod; the dev stage uses alias dev. At 13:10 a teammate deployed an unfinished change to quote-engine to try it in dev. Since then production quotes come back with a currency error. The afternoon merchant settlement run calls the API at 14:30.
handover: The last release, tested and approved, is published as version 41.
Last week someone debugged production by pointing prod at $LATEST 'temporarily'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows API Gateway's stages, the function's aliases and which version each alias points at.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why a test deploy reached production, what you changed, and what prevents it.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The prod alias pointed at $LATEST since a debugging change on 2026-11-10; the 13:10 dev deploy changed $LATEST, and the START lines show every prod request ran it.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: update-alias prod to version 41; the API Gateway integration was untouched. Deleting the alias would have broken the API; publishing version 42 would have frozen the unfinished code.

parts.label: Prevents
parts.modelAnswer: SAM AutoPublishAlias with a CodeDeploy canary, and an IAM deny on pointing prod at $LATEST.

aliasDeleted.headline: Repoint, don't remove
aliasDeleted.body: An alias is the stable name the API calls. Point it at the approved version; deleting it breaks everything that invokes it.

settlementFailed.headline: $LATEST is not an environment
settlementFailed.body: Aliases are environments only when they point at published versions. Production on $LATEST runs whatever was deployed last.

pinned.headline: Good: aliases as environments
pinned.body: You read the alias and the executed versions, repointed prod at the approved version without touching the API, checked the response header, and closed the path that let $LATEST reach production.

scoring.modelReasoning: Production's alias points at $LATEST, so the teammate's dev deploy is serving production. Point the prod alias back at the approved published version 41: the API keeps calling the same alias and nothing else changes. Deleting the alias breaks the API; publishing a new version just freezes the bad code. Then deploy only published versions through AutoPublishAlias and CodeDeploy, and deny $LATEST on prod.
